question: Does source inspection make the Fr 8994 opening-signature lead more specific, and how diagnostic is this signature convention?

source_observation.direct_visual_observation: A small red upper-margin sign has four adjacent vertical strokes, consistent with the MPO catalogue's IIII transcription.
source_observation.not_observed: The image does not independently identify the historical side as recto or verso, and it does not expose a secure reading of the paired k mark.

catalogue_context.record: National Library of Finland, F.m.IV.156, official catalogue description retrieved through search indexing
catalogue_context.finding: The description explains opening signatures as a red small letter on the verso and a Roman numeral on the recto. It says this practice was not infrequent in late-medieval codices and early printed books and points to Antiphoners 34, 157, 170 and 173.
catalogue_context.consequence: The general two-part signature format is not a unique Codex 1505 fingerprint. The exact conjunction of sign, feast, text boundary and sequence remains testable.

source_access.source: Taitto 2001, Fragmenta membranea IV:1, Antiphonaria: text, pp. 161-168
source_access.result: The National Library digital-object route was previously tried and returned Cache miss for the requested pages (E25). The current official Finna metadata identifies a digitized publication associated with Turku, but the normal browser record displayed a Cloudflare verification page. No challenge was interacted with or bypassed; no text pages were obtained.

source_access.source: Jesse Keskiaho 2019, 'En grupp handskrifter från Nådendal: nya rön,' pp. 51-67
source_access.result: The University of Helsinki portal confirms the chapter's bibliographic details. The publisher lists the 2018 volume with 167 pages and a 150 SEK price; no open full-text copy was found in this search. No purchase was made.

source_access.source: Jesse Keskiaho 2008, 'En grupp handskrifter från slutet av 1400-talet – från Nådendals scriptorium?,' pp. 318-350
source_access.result: The University of Helsinki portal and JYKDOK confirm the peer-reviewed article's bibliographic record. The article text was not obtained in this pass.

interpretation.result: The local image now supports the catalogue's four-stroke IIII observation at one region. The official IV.156 catalogue explains that the opening-signature practice is not uncommon, so the form alone is weak evidence of a specific codex. Fr 8994's Olavi content and the IV.157 folio-8 description make a narrow comparison worthwhile, but there is still no paired scan or complete text comparison.
